newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea to deregulate life insurance industry.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea to deregulate life insurance industry.

text.p: South Korea's Ministry of Finance and Economy said on Wednesday it planned to allow the nation's top five business conglomerates, or "chaebols", to participate in the life insurance business.
A ministry statement said it would submit to parliament in June for approval a draft deregulating the life insurance market.
The plan would allow the Hyundai, Daewoo, LG and Sunkyong groups to join the Samsung Group in the sector in the second half of this year.
Currently, Samsung is the only major chaebol which has a life insurance company under its wing.
Under the draft, a new life insurance company must have a minimum paid-in capital of 30 billion won, up from 10 billion at present, the statement said.
The ministry said liberalisation in the insurance sector was planned to strengthen domestic and international competitiveness and to foster healthy management of insurance companies.
